messages.message: ### Step 2: Direct Translation Translate each source line into Spanish, guided by the Reference Translation and Step 1 analysis. Output: ONE Spanish line per source line (preserve line count and end punctuation). Rules: - Follow the meaning from Reference Translation. - For "so X that Y": keep resultative structure, do NOT convert to "because". - No internal punctuation; copy only end punctuation from source.

### Step 3: Word Table & Coverage Check Build a word table from Step 2 translation, mapping each source word to its target equivalent. Output: ONE Markdown table (all lines combined). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Word/Phrase] | [Back-Translation] | [Status: OK/MISSING/WRONG/GRAMMAR/UNNECESSARY] Mark GRAMMAR for agreement errors (gender, number, case) or other grammatical mistakes. Mark UNNECESSARY for elements present in source but not needed in target language (e.g., articles that target language omits naturally). After the table, list any MISSING, WRONG, GRAMMAR, or UNNECESSARY items.

**Word‑to‑Word Alignment Table (Spanish translation of lines 7‑9)**
| Source Word | Contextual Definition (from Step 1) | Target Word / Phrase (Spanish) | Back‑Translation (≈ English) | Status | |-------------|--------------------------------------|--------------------------------|------------------------------|--------| | Tant' | “to such a degree” – intensifier of the predicate | **Tan** | “so / such” | OK | | è | copular verb linking subject to predicate | **es** | “is” | OK | | amara | adjective describing the quality of the subject (bitter) | **amarga** | “bitter” | OK | | che | subordinator introducing result/comparative clause | **que** | “that” | OK | | poco | adverb quantifier indicating slight degree | **poco** | “little / slightly” | OK | | è | copular verb in comparative clause | **es** | “is” | OK | | più | comparative adverb marking increase | **más** | “more” | OK | | morte | noun, the entity being compared (death) | **la muerte** | “the death” | OK | | ; | (punctuation) | **;** | – | – | | ma | coordinating conjunction signalling contrast | **pero** | “but” | OK | | per | preposition marking purpose | **para** | “in order to / for” | OK | | trattar | infinitive verb “to discuss / to treat” | **tratar** | “to treat / to discuss” | OK | | del | contraction *di + il* → “of the” | **del** | “of the” | OK | | ben | noun “good” (the positive thing) | **bien** | “good” | OK | | ch' | relative pronoun introducing clause | **que** | “that / which” | OK | | i' | first‑person pronoun “I” (subject of relative clause) | *(omitted – Spanish drops subject pronoun)* | “I” | **UNNECESSARY** | | vi | locative adverb “there” (place of finding) | **allí** | “there” | OK | | trovai | 1st‑person past “found” | **encontré** | “I found” | OK | | , | (punctuation) | **,** | – | – | | dirò | 1st‑person future “I will tell” | **diré** | “I will say / tell” | OK | | de | preposition introducing complement of *dirò* | **de** | “of / about” | OK | | l'altre | definite article + adjective “the other” (plural) | **las otras** | “the other (feminine plural)” | OK | | cose | noun “things” (plural) | **cosas** | “things” | OK | | ch' | relative pronoun introducing clause | **que** | “that / which” | OK | | i' | first‑person pronoun “I” (subject of perfect) | *(omitted – Spanish drops subject pronoun)* | “I” | **UNNECESSARY** | | v' | clitic locative “there” (part of *v'ho*) | **allí** | “there” | OK | | ho | auxiliary verb “have” (forms perfect) | **he** | “have (aux.)” | OK | | scorte | past participle “seen” | **visto** | “seen” | OK | | . | (punctuation) | **.** | – | – |
---
### Items Requiring Attention - **UNNECESSARY**: - `i'` (twice) – the subject pronoun “I” is omitted in Spanish because the verb inflection already indicates the subject. - **GRAMMAR**: - The clause **“Tan amarga es que la muerte es poco más;”** is syntactically awkward in Spanish; a more natural rendering would be “Tan amarga es que la muerte es poco más.” The current form is acceptable for a literal translation but would be flagged as a minor grammatical oddity.
All other source tokens have appropriate Spanish equivalents and are correctly aligned.

### Step 4: Correction & Final Output Fix any MISSING, WRONG, or GRAMMAR items from Step 3. Reorder within line if needed; do not add new content words. Verify that the output contains only Spanish script; no other language scripts should be mixed in. Output format (use nested bullet list, not table): - Line N: - Original: ... - Issue: ... (or "none") - Corrected: ... (or "no change") Output final Spanish text in ONE code block, line by line (no extra prose).

- **Line 7** - Original: Tan amarga **es** que la muerte es poco más; - Issue: GRAMMAR – the copula “es” after “amarga” makes the clause unidiomatic. - Corrected: Tan amarga que la muerte es poco más;
- **Line 8** - Original: pero para tratar del bien que allí encontré, - Issue: none - Corrected: no change
- **Line 9** - Original: diré de las otras cosas que allí he visto. - Issue: none - Corrected: no change
```text Tan amarga que la muerte es poco más; pero para tratar del bien que allí encontré, diré de las otras cosas que allí he visto. ```
